title: Per-token latency ledger and cache-delta tagging for cost & SLO attribution
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Goal: produce a minimal-overhead, production-safe per-token ledger that records micro-timings (emit, decode, kernel, io) and a cache-delta tag (cache_hit|cache_miss|cache_stale) so we can attribute latency and cost at token granularity for billing reconciliation, SLO analysis, and adaptive routing. This ticket covers: 1) span/metric schema and runtime hooks in the serving engine, 2) OTLP -> Kafka ingestion path and ClickHouse aggregation schema, 3) rollout/sampling strategy and perf guardrails, and 4) dashboard + alerting for token-level regressions. The ledger must be queryable by request-id, model, route, and token index and joinable with existing cost tables.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits per-token OTel spans with required attributes (request_id, model, route, seq_index, phase, kernel_ms, decode_ms, kv_cache_status)
End-to-end ingestion can handle 1% global traffic with <10% CPU/mem overhead on p50 worker and <0.5ms added p50 latency per request
ClickHouse table schema supports efficient aggregations for per-route p50/p90 token latency and cache-hit delta calculations
Console dashboard shows token-level latency breakdown and cache hit impact, with a regression alert when token p90 increases by >10% vs baseline
Billing join computes per-token cost delta within 5% of offline simulation for a sampled workload
Feature gated rollout can be controlled per-customer and per-model, and sampling rate adjustable without deploys
steps: Define OTel span/metric contract and attribute names with privacy check
Implement lightweight hooks in Rust/C++ serving runtime to emit token spans and a summarizing request span
Add a kv_cache_status enum {hit, miss, stale, not_present} and include a ttl_warmth tag when possible
Instrument OTEL collector to batch and forward token spans to Kafka (topic: telemetry.tokens) with compression
Create ClickHouse tables and materialized views for fast per-route aggregations; add retention policy (30d raw, 365d aggregates)
Build Console dashboard panels and Looker/Metabase queries for billing team
Roll out with progressive sampling: 0.05% -> 0.5% -> 1% per-model with circuit breaker if overhead > threshold
Run canary on internal product routes and compare attributed costs vs offline estimator

notes: Design tradeoffs: full-token logging gives best fidelity but high throughput cost. We choose sampled spans plus an aggregated request-level summary span for un-sampled requests.
Aggregation strategy: use ClickHouse materialized views to maintain p50/p90 by (model, route, seq_bucket) where seq_bucket groups token index into 0-7,8-15,16+ for efficient storage
Billing join: store a per-token unit cost table keyed by model+quantization_profile; compute cost_delta = token_cost * (1 - cache_effectiveness_factor)
Open questions: whether to include kv_cache_hotness score (recently used in same request) vs global warming metric. Proposed to add later as optional attribute.
Fallbacks: if Kafka ingestion lags, fall back to sampling fewer spans and rely on request-level summaries to keep dashboards meaningful
